name: Terrell Bailey-Corsey
bio: Terrell Bailey-Corsey was arrested on July 18, 2025 after federal prosecutors alleged that he posted threats to kill politicians, government officials, and people associated with Jeffrey Epstein. He was initially detained, then released on August 20, 2025 to live with his grandparents under home detention and electronic monitoring. The charges remain allegations and no conviction has been established.
sources: Court Watch report on the arrest
Federal order documenting detention and release

case.charges: Two counts of transmitting interstate threats against a current or former government official.
case.indicted: Yes — federally indicted on two threat counts.
case.sentence: No sentence; released under restrictive pretrial conditions.

name: Abdullah Haji Zada
bio: Abdullah Haji Zada was arrested on October 7, 2024 with Nasir Ahmad Tawhedi in an undercover operation concerning an ISIS-inspired Election Day attack plan. Zada, who was 17 at the time of arrest, later pleaded guilty as an adult to receiving and conspiring to receive firearms and ammunition for a federal terrorism crime. He was sentenced on November 19, 2025 to the statutory maximum of fifteen years in federal prison.
sources: Associated Press report on the sentence

case.charges: Knowingly receiving, attempting to receive, and conspiring to receive firearms and ammunition for use in a federal crime of terrorism.
case.sentence: Fifteen years in federal prison, followed by removal to Afghanistan.

name: Ammaad Akhtar
bio: Ammaad Akhtar was arrested in Stockton, California, on June 24, 2025. Federal prosecutors allege that he sent money to people he believed were associated with ISIS, discussed violent attacks, pledged allegiance to the organization, and delivered cash, clothing, binoculars, two loaded guns, and magazines to an undercover employee. He remains detained while awaiting trial, and the allegations have not been proved.
sources: Federal order setting the November 2026 trial

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS.

name: Dale Britt Bendler
bio: Dale Britt Bendler, a retired CIA officer who later returned as a contractor, pleaded guilty to acting as an undisclosed foreign agent while a public official and mishandling classified material. Prosecutors said he used classified systems to assist private foreign clients and influence public policy while earning hundreds of thousands of dollars. He began serving two concurrent one-year-and-one-day sentences on January 5, 2026 and was released on August 13, 2026.

case.charges: Acting as a foreign agent while a public official and unauthorized removal and retention of classified material.
case.sentence: Two concurrent terms of one year and one day in federal prison.

name: Rex Crofton
bio: Rex Crofton was arrested on June 3, 2026 after allegedly smashing the entry doors of Congregation Albert and the Jewish Community Center in Albuquerque and sending messages boasting about the attacks and threatening police. A federal judge ordered him detained after federal agents arrested him as he was about to leave state custody. The federal hate-crime case remains pending and the allegations have not been proved.
sources: New Mexico Jewish Journal case chronology

case.charges: Damage to religious property, with federal prosecutors alleging attacks on a synagogue and Jewish community center.

name: Mansuri Manuchekhri
bio: Mansuri Manuchekhri was arrested in Brooklyn on February 26, 2025. Federal prosecutors allege that he facilitated more than $50,000 in payments to ISIS-affiliated people, praised ISIS attacks, collected violent propaganda, trained with firearms, and committed immigration fraud. His motions were still being litigated in 2026; he remains detained pending trial, and the allegations have not been proved.
sources: Federal court order on pretrial motions

case.charges: Conspiracy to provide material support to ISIS and ISIS-K, unlawful firearm possession, immigration fraud, and a false statement charge.

name: Mark Tucci
bio: Mark Tucci pleaded guilty to federal civil-rights, cyberstalking, and threat charges after a campaign of racist threats directed at Black residents and a Philadelphia city employee. The conduct included repeated racial epithets, threats to kill or injure people, messages identifying a victim's home street, and a separate road incident. He was sentenced on December 2, 2025 to thirty-three months in federal prison.

case.charges: Interfering with federally protected activities, cyberstalking, and interstate communication of threats.
case.convicted: Yes — federal civil-rights, cyberstalking, and threat offenses.
case.sentence: Thirty-three months in federal prison, two years of supervised release, and restitution.

name: Carter Miles Ledoux
bio: Carter Miles Ledoux was arrested in February 2026 and federally indicted on allegations that he participated in a nihilistic violent extremist group, stalked and threatened a minor because she expressed support for interracial relationships, helped place a hoax emergency call targeting her family, and possessed child sexual abuse material. The Fifth Circuit affirmed the order detaining him before trial in May 2026. The allegations have not been proved.

case.charges: Conspiracy, stalking, threats, swatting, and a separate charge of possessing child sexual abuse material.
case.indicted: Yes — two federal indictments returned February 18, 2026.
